lines.text: Describing someone's physical appearance is an essential skill in English. People come in many shapes and sizes. A person may be tall, short, or of average height. Their build can be slim, athletic, stocky, plump, or muscular. We describe faces using adjectives like oval, round, square, or heart-shaped. Eyes can be described by color — blue, brown, green, hazel, or grey — and by shape, such as almond-shaped, round, or narrow. Eyebrows may be thick, thin, arched, or bushy. Noses are described as straight, pointed, flat, or button-shaped. Lips can be thin, full, or bow-shaped. A person's complexion refers to the tone and condition of their skin: fair, olive, dark, tanned, freckled, or pale. Hair is described by color (blonde, brunette, auburn, red, grey, black), by texture (straight, wavy, curly, coarse, fine), and by length (long, short, shoulder-length, cropped). Facial hair includes a beard, mustache, goatee, sideburns, or stubble. Someone can be described as attractive, plain, or striking. A scar, a mole, or a birthmark might be a distinguishing feature. Learning to describe appearance politely and accurately is important in daily conversation, especially when identifying someone or giving a description.

lines.text: In English, some appearance words are sensitive. Avoid 'fat', 'ugly', 'skinny'. Use neutral terms: 'curvy', 'full-figured', 'slender', 'petite'. 'Tall' and 'short' are acceptable; 'big' and 'small' for people are not.
lines.name: In English, some appearance words are sensitive. Avoid 'fat', 'ugly', 'skinny'. Use neutral terms: 'curvy', 'full-figured', 'slender', 'petite'. 'Tall' and 'short' are acceptable; 'big' and 'small' for people are not.

lines.text: 'Handsome' is typically used for men, 'beautiful' for women, but 'attractive', 'good-looking', and 'striking' work for anyone. 'Pretty' is usually for women/girls; 'cute' is informal and gender-neutral.
lines.name: 'Handsome' is typically used for men, 'beautiful' for women, but 'attractive', 'good-looking', and 'striking' work for anyone. 'Pretty' is usually for women/girls; 'cute' is informal and gender-neutral.

lines.text: 'Blonde' (light), 'brunette' (brown), 'auburn' (reddish-brown), 'ginger/red' (red). These originally come from French. 'Blonde' can also refer to the person: 'She is a blonde.'
lines.name: 'Blonde' (light), 'brunette' (brown), 'auburn' (reddish-brown), 'ginger/red' (red). These originally come from French. 'Blonde' can also refer to the person: 'She is a blonde.'

lines.text: Use tone-neutral terms: 'fair', 'light', 'medium', 'olive', 'dark', 'deep'. Avoid comparing skin to food (chocolate, caramel). 'Tanned' means sun-darkened, not a permanent skin color.
